method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb autoregressive SMILES policy optimization
method_thesis: Pretrain an autoregressive SMILES language model on the allowed unlabeled corpus and freeze a copy as the molecular prior. During each objective session, sample complete molecules de novo token by token from a trainable agent, rank the accepted molecules by their observed oracle rewards, and update the agent only on the highest-reward fraction using the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: the squared gap between agent log-likelihood and a target formed from prior log-likelihood plus scaled reward. Excluding low-reward samples from policy updates prevents them from repeatedly pulling the agent back toward the prior, while prior likelihood still regularizes the elite updates; this concentrates the scarce feedback on sequences associated with improvement of final Top-1 without screening a finite molecular pool.

method_tags.proposal_mechanism: ancestral token sampling from an online reward-conditioned molecular policy

activation_observables.measurement: For every preparation seed, record each epoch's token NLL, fixed-stream completed count, unique valid canonical count, state digest, and deterministic selection rank. On a disjoint fixed audit stream of 256 ancestral draws, evaluate the selected checkpoint and the terminal epoch-five checkpoint with common random numbers and report their unique-valid rates and selected-minus-terminal difference, while verifying that the published weight digest equals the selected digest. Parent n-6174d6127af5 has no checkpoint choice and therefore a selection lift of 0.0; activation requires reconstructible selection and a positive pooled selected-minus-terminal audit-rate change across the assigned preparation seeds.

applicability_conditions: The five fixed pretraining epochs contain at least one checkpoint whose task-agnostic ancestral support is better than the terminal checkpoint; when support improves monotonically through epoch five, the selector should retain the Parent behavior and provides no expected gain.

The fixed label-free selection probe ranks checkpoint support well enough that its winner also improves the disjoint common-random-number audit; a 256-draw probe can be noisy when checkpoints have nearly identical valid yield.

Completion and unique canonical validity are useful preparation-time proxies for the downstream policy's ability to fill novel batches; they do not establish that the sampled support contains reward-reachable chemistry for every objective.

All checkpoints share the same corpus-derived vocabulary, special-token indices, maximum length, and architecture, so choosing an earlier state does not alter the published artifact interface or any downstream token identity.

Selection remains strictly preparation-local and task agnostic: it uses only ancestral samples, RDKit validity and canonical identity, and training NLL, never task identity, initial observations, oracle scores, or state from another preparation.

The evidence motivating the intervention covers three preparations of this corpus and model schedule; transfer to another corpus, architecture, training duration, or support probe size requires a new comparison.
research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism did not happen if the recorded epoch probes and tie breakers do not reconstruct the selected checkpoint, if the published state digest differs from that checkpoint, or if any task identity or oracle observation enters selection. If those wiring checks pass but the pooled held-out selected-minus-terminal prior unique-valid-rate change is not positive, the claim that support-aware checkpoint selection improves the intermediate ancestral support is falsified even if a nonterminal epoch was published.
research_intent.implementation_change: Keep the corpus reservoir, tokenizer and vocabulary, model dimensions, optimizer, learning rate, regularization, five training epochs, preparation seed, and every run-mode Layer unchanged. After each existing epoch, snapshot the model state and evaluate it in inference mode on the same fixed 256-draw task-agnostic selection stream. Rank epoch checkpoints first by unique-valid count, then by completed count, then by lower recorded token NLL and later epoch as deterministic tie breakers. Retain only the leading checkpoint, while allowing training to continue unchanged through epoch five. At the end, use a second fixed preparation-only common-random-number audit stream to measure both the selected and terminal checkpoints, publish exactly the selected state through the existing smiles_prior.pt and smiles_policy.json interface, and add selection epoch, checkpoint digests, per-epoch probe measurements, and paired audit measurements to preparation diagnostics and configuration metadata.
research_intent.mechanism: Replace blind terminal-epoch publication with label-free ancestral-support checkpoint selection inside the unchanged five-epoch corpus pretraining run: retain the epoch whose fixed preparation-only probe produces the highest unique-valid fraction, and publish that epoch's model state as the frozen prior.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: Parent n-6174d6127af5 always publishes the fifth and final pretraining epoch after only one terminal 256-draw support check and a permissive unique-valid-rate threshold of 0.01, so it cannot reject a late checkpoint whose corpus likelihood improved while its ancestral chemical support worsened. That missing selection step matters because the three independently prepared Parent artifacts show seed-sensitive support: prior unique-valid rate ranges from 0.8125 to 0.85546875, online complete-conditioned novel-valid yield ranges from 0.7832720190434971 to 0.8541171385346877, vocabulary size ranges from 74 to 78, and seed-level macro score ranges from 0.498752613558053 to 0.544472616912355. These paired variations do not prove that the terminal checkpoint caused the score spread, but they identify blind final-epoch publication as the active-layer behavior that leaves the weakest prepared artifact unprotected.

applicability_conditions: The confirmed activation applies to the evaluated 250,000-example unlabeled-corpus preparations, corpus-derived vocabularies, fixed GRU architecture and optimizer, five-epoch schedule, three preparation seeds, and separate 256-draw selection and audit streams.

The mechanism has an opportunity to improve support only when a nonterminal checkpoint outranks epoch five on the task-agnostic probe. That condition occurred on seed 1; on seeds 0 and 2 the selector correctly retained epoch five and produced exactly zero selected-minus-terminal audit change.

Observed benefit further requires the fixed selection probe to rank support in a way that transfers to the disjoint audit. Seed 1 satisfied that condition, with epoch 4 ahead of epoch 5 on both streams, but the modest count margins do not establish reliable ranking for near-tied checkpoints outside these replicas.

Selection remains preparation-local and label-free in the observed implementation, and all checkpoints within a preparation share one vocabulary, special-token mapping, maximum length, and architecture. All three selected artifacts loaded through the frozen two-file interface and supported all 15 complete downstream sessions.

The evidence supports improved held-out unique-valid ancestral yield, not improved objective score or reward-reachable chemical coverage. Transfer to another corpus, model, training duration, or support metric requires a new paired comparison.

applicability_conditions: The five fixed pretraining epochs contain at least one checkpoint whose task-agnostic ancestral support is better than the terminal checkpoint; when support improves monotonically through epoch five, the selector should retain the Parent behavior and provides no expected gain.

The fixed label-free selection probe ranks checkpoint support well enough that its winner also improves the disjoint common-random-number audit; a 256-draw probe can be noisy when checkpoints have nearly identical valid yield.

Completion and unique canonical validity are useful preparation-time proxies for the downstream policy's ability to fill novel batches; they do not establish that the sampled support contains reward-reachable chemistry for every objective.

All checkpoints share the same corpus-derived vocabulary, special-token indices, maximum length, and architecture, so choosing an earlier state does not alter the published artifact interface or any downstream token identity.

Selection remains strictly preparation-local and task agnostic: it uses only ancestral samples, RDKit validity and canonical identity, and training NLL, never task identity, initial observations, oracle scores, or state from another preparation.

The evidence motivating the intervention covers three preparations of this corpus and model schedule; transfer to another corpus, architecture, training duration, or support probe size requires a new comparison.
